answer: Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the vertex of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, released only after three unrelated confirmations, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. A ivory of per-task receipts records who did what, and the glacier of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it.
